title: 2027 BMW iX3 M60 tanıtıldı: 603 beygir güç sunan yeni elektrikli SUV
summary: BMW'nin yeni performans odaklı elektrikli SUV modeli 2027 BMW iX3 M60, çift elektrik motoruyla 603 beygir güç ve 3,9 saniyede 0-100 km/s hızlanma sunuyor.
body:
Motor1 ve Car and Driver'ın aktardığına göre, **2027 BMW iX3 M60** markanın tamamen elektrikli yeni SUV ailesinin en tepe performans versiyonu olarak resmiyet kazandı. Çift elektrik motoruyla donatılan araç, toplamda **603 beygir** güç ve 874 Nm (645 pound-fit) tork üretiyor. Araç, 0'dan yaklaşık 100 kilometre hıza (62 mph) 3,9 saniyede ulaşabiliyor ve azami hızı saatte 238 kilometreye (149 mil) çıkıyor.

## Gelişmiş donanım ve teknik özellikler

Model, BMW'nin altıncı nesil M eDrive sistemini ve 112,2 kWh kullanılabilir kapasiteye sahip büyük bir batarya paketini kullanıyor. Car and Driver'ın belirttiğine göre araç, 800 voltluk elektrik mimarisi sayesinde 400 kW şarj hızını destekliyor. Öte yandan Motor1'in haberinde, aracın sürüş tepkilerini önceki nesillere göre çok daha hızlı koordine eden yeni "Heart of Joy" işlemcisine sahip olduğu vurgulanıyor. Donanım tarafında ise adaptif M süspansiyon, elektronikte kontrollü M Sport diferansiyel, değişken oranlı spor direksiyon ve standart 21 inç jantlar yer alıyor. İç mekanda ise sürücüye dönük 17.9 inçlik merkezi ekran, Operating System X ve Harman Kardon ses sistemi bulunuyor.

## Çıkış takvimi ve beklentiler

BMW'nin duyurusuna göre, yeni performans SUV'sinin üretimi 2027 baharında Macaristan'daki fabrikada başlayacak ve siparişler ocak ayının sonunda açılacak. Kaynaklar, resmi fiyatlandırma ve EPA menzil verilerinin henüz açıklanmadığını, ancak aracın satış tarihi yaklaşırken netleşeceğini belirtiyor.

**Neden önemli?** Tamamen elektrikli performans SUV segmentindeki rekabeti artıran model, gelişmiş sürüş dinamikleri ve yeni nesil teknolojileriyle markanın elektrikli araç dönüşümünde önemli bir basamağı temsil ediyor.

source_texts.title: BMW's Newest Performance SUV Packs 603 Horsepower
source_texts.summary: BMW's range-topping iX3 M60 packs dual motors, 645 lb-ft of torque, and a 149-mph top speed.
source_texts.text:
BMW's Newest Performance SUV Packs 603 Horsepower
BMW's range-topping iX3 M60 packs dual motors, 645 lb-ft of torque, and a 149-mph top speed.
BMW is already turning up the wick on its newest SUV. The 2027 BMW iX3 M60 debuts as the range-topping version of the brand’s new all-electric SUV, packing 603 horsepower, 645 pound-feet of torque, and a 0-62 mile-per-hour time of just 3.9 seconds.
And it’s not just power. The M Performance model also brings a more aggressive chassis setup, M-specific styling, and the automaker's latest electric-drive technology. Production is scheduled to begin in spring 2027, with orders opening at the end of January.
As the name should tell you, this isn’t a full-blown M car. Still, the new M60 model gets plenty of hardware designed to make this version of the iX3 considerably more fun to drive than the standard model.
The iX3 M60 uses BMW's sixth-generation M eDrive system, with an electric motor powering each axle. The rear motor is a new electrically excited synchronous unit with a more powerful 420-amp inverter, helping deliver that extra oomph.
Here are the numbers:
- Output: 603 HP / 645 LB-FT
- 0-62 MPH: 3.9 Seconds
- Top speed: 149 MPH
- Battery: 112.2 kWh (Usable)
BMW hasn't announced an EPA range figure yet, but expect a slight decrease from the non-performance variant. The standard iX3 gets up to 434 miles of range in the US.
Not only is the iX3 M60’s battery bigger, but the new "Heart of Joy" processor improves driving-related inputs up to 10 times faster than the systems used in its previous-generation vehicles. It works alongside BMW M Dynamic Performance Control to coordinate the powertrain, braking, steering, and regenerative braking systems.
There are also dedicated Boost and M Mode controls on the steering wheel, along with M-specific displays and additional driving settings. The M60 gets two exclusive My Modes: M Sport and M Sport Plus. They adjust the powertrain, chassis, and steering for increasingly aggressive responses.
BMW also says the iX3's regenerative braking system can handle nearly all everyday deceleration. Its Soft Stop function uses regenerative braking to bring the SUV to a smooth stop without the conventional braking feel or noise.
The M60 gets more than cosmetic upgrades. BMW fitted the SUV with Adaptive M Suspension, electronically controlled dampers, variable-ratio sport steering, and an electronically controlled M Sport differential at the rear axle.
The chassis also receives model-specific spring and damper tuning, stiffer front-end bracing, and revised anti-roll-bar links designed to improve steering precision and reduce body roll.
The standard setup includes:
- Adaptive M Suspension with electronically controlled dampers
- Variable-ratio M Sport steering
- Electronically controlled M Sport differential
- Model-specific springs and dampers
- Revised front-axle anti-roll-bar links
- Additional front-end bracing
- Standard 21-inch M alloy wheels
M Sport brakes with red or blue calipers are available as an option. The iX3 M60 can also be fitted with 21-inch sport tires developed specifically for the model, while 22-inch M aerodynamic wheels are available exclusively on the M Performance version.
BMW has given the M60 several visual changes to distinguish it from lesser iX3 models. The SUV comes standard with the M Sport package and BMW Iconic Glow exterior lighting. The optional M Yellow Lights, meanwhile, are inspired by BMW's race cars.
The front lighting signature also incorporates three elements inspired by BMW's familiar M stripes, along with an illuminated M logo. Elsewhere, the M60 gets standard 21-inch wheels (with 22-inch options), M-specific mirror caps, a black rear diffuser, and more.
Inside, the iX3 M60 gets BMW's latest Panoramic iDrive interface and Operating System X. A 17.9-inch central display is angled toward the driver, while BMW Panoramic Vision projects information across the lower portion of the windshield.
The M Sport steering wheel gets a red 12 o'clock marker and dedicated controls for Boost Mode and M Mode. Drivers can also select the M Sport and M Sport Plus settings directly from the wheel.
M Sport seats are available with aggressive side bolsters, 10-way power adjustment, lumbar support, adjustable thigh support, backrest-width adjustment, and massage functionality. The illuminated M logo is integrated into the headrests.
The standard M interior uses black Veganza upholstery with M PerformTex. Buyers can also choose more upscale Contemporary and BMW Individual interior configurations. BMW's standard 13-speaker Harman Kardon audio system produces 430 watts and supports Dolby Atmos.
Production starts in spring 2027, with US orders opening at the end of January. BMW has not yet announced pricing or official EPA range for the 2027 iX3 M60. We should know all the details closer to the on-sale date.

source_texts.title: 2027 BMW iX3 M60 Joins the EV SUV Party Packing 603 HP
source_texts.summary: BMW adds a high-performance version of the iX3 that hits 62 mph in a claimed 3.9 seconds.
source_texts.text:
- The 2027 BMW iX3 lineup is adding an M60 performance model that features a standard 603-hp all-wheel-drive powertrain.
- BMW claims the new iX3 M60 can accelerate to 62 mph in 3.9 seconds on its way to a 149-mph top speed; its EPA-estimated driving range has not been released yet.
- The iX3 M60 will be available to order in January 2027, though we’re still waiting to hear from BMW about how much it will cost.
If you’re interested in BMW’s new electric compact luxury SUV, but the existing iX3 50 isn’t spicy enough for your tastes, the menu is about to expand to include a high-performance variant that features the brand’s iconic M badge. To be clear, the 2027 BMW iX3 M60 isn’t a full-blown M car. While it’s a step below that tier, it still looks to have the bona fides to get your blood pumping after unplugging it from the charger.
Whereas the iX3 50 xDrive features dual electric motors that send 463 horsepower and 476 pound-feet of torque to all four wheels, the iX3 M60 pushes those figures to 603 ponies and 645 pound-feet. BMW says the increase comes from an enhanced rear-mounted electric motor that features a new stator and a more powerful inverter. Along with a higher max rotor speed, the M60 has a longer gear ratio that enables a top speed of 149 mph (up from 130 mph). BMW claims the mightier iX3 can hit 62 mph in 3.9 seconds—a full second quicker than its less powerful sibling.
Both the iX3 50 xDrive and M60 xDrive share an 800-volt electrical system, including a 112-kWh battery pack. Likewise, their charging rate peaks at 400 kW, and while the 50 has an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 434 miles, we’ll have to wait a bit to find out how far the M60 can travel on a full charge. Considering it comes with standard 21-inch wheels, though, that final estimate will be under 400 miles, and the optional 22-inchers will drop the range even lower.
You’ll be able to tell an M60 from the other iX3 by its rear badge, of course, but also its roof spoiler and unique lighting signatures. The front incorporates the M logo as well as a three-element motif, and customers can also opt for yellow lights that are a nod to BMW’s motorsports pedigree. But the iX3 M60 has the hardware to back up its sporty visual flourishes. That includes a specially tuned suspension with adaptive dampers, variable steering ratio, upgraded brakes, and an electronically controlled rear diff. Its dynamic systems are also managed by BMW's “Heart of Joy superbrain,” a newly developed consolidated control unit that’s found on every Neue Klasse EV.
Inside, drivers get to experience BMW’s new futuristic dashboard layout, which essentially turns what would traditionally be found in a gauge cluster into a pillar-to-pillar display. Along with an optional 3-D head-up display, you can choose to outfit your iX3 M60 with front sport seats that’ll better hug you during hard cornering. You won’t have to pay extra for the 17.9-inch hexagonal touchscreen that looks like it’s leaning toward the driver. BMW also spruces up the M60’s cabin with M-specific details, such as the steering wheel with dedicated buttons for Boost and customizable drive modes. And for those who like to rock, a 13-speaker Harman Kardon sound system that supports Dolby Atmos is standard. Provided you’re on a highway and don’t need to exceed 85 mph, the iX3 offers hands-free driving, but the SAE Level 2 system still requires you keep your eyes on the road.
The 2027 BMW iX3 M60 will be available to order sometime at the end of January next year, with production slated to start at BMW’s Hungary factory in the spring. We should find out how much it costs between now and then, but considering the iX3 50 currently starts at $62,850, we wouldn’t be surprised if the high-performance model surpasses $70K.

Eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive new cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.
